speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That information regarding the brother and the appendicitis diagnosis seems unusual for a newborn; can you clarify the family history of liver disease and confirm the exact age of the infant in days? REQUEST TEST: Coombs_Direct_Test. REQUEST TEST: G6PD_Activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Crigler-Najjar Syndrome Type II. The normal Coombs test, normal G6PD activity, exclusive breastfeeding history, and significant hyperbilirubinemia in a newborn with a family history of liver surgery strongly suggest an enzymatic defect in bilirubin conjugation, specifically UDP-glucuronosyltransferase deficiency. I will need to review liver function panel results to confirm. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.
